new.n: Abbotsford depot express robbery: $9,000 never found
new.pl: Abbotsford (Clark Co.); depot not placed; the woods toward Colby are too vague to search
new.v: About $9,000 in express money and two jewelry packages
new.st: Night operator Eugene McNally was convicted of taking about $9,000 from the depot safe at Abbotsford on 18 May 1891: $8,000 sent by the Seymour Bank, Chippewa Falls, to the State Bank of Phillips, about $1,000 more and two jewelry packages (Northern Pacific Express). His footprints were found under the depot the next morning, "very likely seeking a safe hiding place", and he was in the woods that morning walking to Colby. He got 5 years at Waupun, and "the money has never been found". In June 1892 a rumor said it had been found buried near Abbotsford, with a local family "very flush with money". The pin marks Abbotsford, not the depot.
new.t: Likely dug up in 1892 (rumor). The depot grounds are railroad land: look only.
src: Marshfield News, 24 Dec 1891, p. 1 (newspapers.com 266221023) and 16 Jun 1892, p. 4 (266228994)
pinev: Town of Abbotsford only; the depot is not placed
